GERMAN — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Wasser
   B. Haus
   C. Schule
   D. Buch

2. When practising Reading aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading aloud.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading aloud.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading aloud.

3. When practising Reading Aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud.

4. When practising Guided writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Guided writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Guided writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Guided writing.

5. When practising Phonological awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological awareness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological awareness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness.

6. When practising Reading for comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for comprehension.

7. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good night
   C. Please
   D. Good day / hello

8. When practising Listening for gist, Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist, Imitative speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist, Imitative speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist, Imitative speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist, Imitative speaking.

9. When practising Guided reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Guided reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Guided reading.

10. When practising Listening for gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for gist and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological awareness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for gist, Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
